setupContract.audience: DPH-4 harness only. The scorer and the contract validator do not read `setup`, `setupContract` or `steps`; they are bound by the freeze record because they are part of the fixture bytes.
rules: Run each variant in its own workspace (workspace namespace = isolation.workspaceId + '/' + variantId).

Order inside a stage: case.setup writes (project, tree, Scope, Codex) and the variant's own codexEntities first; then the steps in the listed order. A stage-2 `binding-change` is the only write after the first prepare of stage 1; it precedes the first prepare of stage 2.

Every prepare/approve/write goes through the product writer named in the draft's list (receipt.mjs EVENT_KIND_WRITERS): prepare = nir1_entity_relation_revision_prepare, approve and decision-cancel = narrative_extraction_append_human_decision, codex-update = codex_update, scene-scope-registry-update = narrative_scene_scope_registry_update. No direct DML.

The negative (reject variants of ordinary cases) is prepared, approved, then invalidated before any positive Revision is prepared (checkSetupCase: prepare-negative < approve-negative < invalidate-negative < first prepare).
Chat sessions are created with the renderer's createSession statement (node_id = the query Scene) before the profile is restricted; one per stage.
The user message of the case is the captured human message of every stage.

A placeholder `{{kind:logicalId}}` resolves from the setup receipt: runtimeId = idMap runtimeId (project, Scene, Codex Entity); revisionId/proposalId/decisionId = idMap rows of the Revision; revisionToken/sourceToken = runtimeValues rows (see each variant's setup.runtimeValues).
Read a runtimeValues row after the stage's last write and invalidation and before its capture; it is never read from a request's output.

writers.projectAndScenes: tree writers (tree_node_create with a single-paragraph ProseMirror body, or save_scene_body_bundle); the Scene body text is the Raw
writers.sceneScope: narrative_scene_scope_registry_update (registry first), then narrative_scene_scope_update for every Scene
writers.codex: codex_create (type, name, summary), codex_update for a summary change
writers.route: write_ai_settings: provider openai-compatible, one endpoint fixture-local at http://127.0.0.1:12345/v1 (loopback, no request is sent), customMaxContext and customMaxOutput from `route`, model from `route.model`
writers.prepare: nir1_entity_relation_revision_prepare { projectId, sceneId: the anchor Scene, entityIds: [the Entity], relationIds: [], proposalKey }

setupContract.scopeNotes: Every Scene (anchor and query) gets the same explicit Scope; the anchor precedes the query in reading order (the A3 gate needs reading_rank(anchor) < reading_rank(query)). `addTimelineRef` adds that reference to the registry only; no Scene Scope is changed.

decisionPayload.cancel: a single human cancellation: decision `rejected` on a revision whose only Decision is `approved`

setupContract.evidenceRule: A prepared Entity's Evidence quote is the Codex summary verbatim (the name when the summary is blank). summaries below are non-blank, trimmed, single-line, and contain no JSON-escaped character.
